newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks down but off lows at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks down but off lows at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were down but off their lows at midday amid profit-taking following Tuesday's rally and renewed softness in the bond market.
Intel Corp shares failed to take flight today despite a strong earnings report after Tuesday's closing bell which saw profits more than double in the fourth quarter.
Instead, the stock, which yesterday spearheaded a high tech rally, was down 2-1/8 at 145 in very active trading.
The Dow was down 39 points at 6722 while declines led advances by 13 to nine on volume of about 224 million shares.
The Dow had slid more than 50 points to 6704, triggering the New York Stock Exchange's curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 1100 EST/1600 GMT.

The Nasdaq Composite Index, heavily weighted with high tech issues, was down seven points at 1340. U.S. Treasuries were mostly down but off their lows, with the long bond falling 9/32 to yield 6.79 percent.

"Bonds had a good day yesterday and that gave rise to a rally in the stock market," said George Pirrone, senior trader at Dreyfus Corp. "Today, bonds are down and Intel is not shining the way people hoped it would this morning."

"This is a very volatile market. We are beginning to look a little worn out in the averages in the sense that right below all the good things we have been seeing are underpinnings that look lackluster," Pirrone said.
"Many stocks are just rallying to their old highs. Breadth was good yesterday but was mediocre for several days before that. These are the warning signs of a small pullback."
The decline in shares of Intel and some other high techs was due to the fact that the sector had a strong run yesterday in anticipation of the Intel quarter, analysts said.
Other high tech stocks under pressure included, International Business Machines Corp, down 1/4 at 166-5/8 and Microsoft Corp, down 1/8 at 85-1/4.

"The high techs are used as a trading vehicle. When the economy looks like it's growing they are bought, and when it comes time to take profits they are the first to be sold out of a portfolio," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities. "Part of the overall drop in the market is profit-taking. There is a sentiment that things are so good that they can't possibly get any better. Where do we go from here? Might as well take profits," she said.

Among today's special situations, Tencor Instruments was up 6-5/8 at 37-1/8 after the company announced last night it agreed to be acquired by KLA Instruments Corp in a one-for-one stock swap. KLA shares were down 1/2 at 40-3/8.
Baan Co NV was up 2-1/2 at 44 in U.S. trading after Salomon Brothers said it raised its rating on the stock to buy from hold.
SoundView Financial group said it raised its earnings estimate for Intel in fiscal 1997 to $8.75 per share from $7.92 per share.
The estimate for fiscal 1998 was raised to $10.60 from $10.00 per share. It kept its rating unchanged at short- and long-term buy.
